rejectedEdges.reason: The text for n-16-2 concerns infant mortality in foundling systems vs. natural family rearing, while n-16-3 critiques Plato's mistaken admiration of Sparta's suppression of individuality. While both are critical of Plato's institutions, neither passage establishes a grounding or 'supports' relation between them.

Node n-17-1 deals with simplicity and prevention in medicine and law, which does not directly develop into or form the basis of the metaphysical dialectic and the idea of the good in n-17-2 (as confirmed by the cited passage p-500166, which refers to training in music and gymnastic, not medicine and law).

value.notes: Reviewed target nodes and edges against cited evidence. Nodes accurately reflect their cited texts, structural levels, and thematic groupings. Edge e-16-1 was rejected because the two critiques are topical parallels rather than an evidential or supportive relation. Edge e-17-1 was rejected because medicine/law simplicity does not develop dialectic/Idea of Good.
